      Eagles end streak against Heritage

      By Richard Greene
      on September 14, 2019

      FacebookTwitterEmailMessengerCopy LinkMessageShare
      Listen to audio version of this article
      Sponsored by
      0:00 / 3:09
      Instaread

      Playing a team they had never beaten, the Decatur Eagles’ night got off to an ominous start when Midlothian Heritage returned the opening kickoff to the Eagles’ 35.

      But it didn’t take long for the Eagles to turn things around. Getting the first of three turnovers and then riding a red-hot start from quarterback Roman Fuller, Decatur continued its unbeaten streak to start the season.

      Decatur built a two-touchdown halftime lead and put Heritage away in the second half of a 41-28 victory at Eagle Stadium Friday night to move to 3-0.

      A.J. Martinez runs the ball against Midlothian Heritage Friday at Eagle Stadium. Messenger photo by Richard Greene

      “We’re happy with that, but as soon as we get done with film tomorrow, our focus will be getting to 1-0 next week and staying hungry,” said Decatur coach Mike Fuller. “We just need to keep working as hard as we can to be as good as we possibly can.”

      After losing to Heritage the past three years, including a 56-21 setback last season, the Eagles played with a hunger Friday. Roman Fuller and junior David Juarez led the way. Fuller connected on his first nine passes, including scoring tosses of 37 and 10 yards to Juarez.

      The 37-yard strike ended the Eagles’ first drive. Juarez caught eight passes for 118 yards.

      Fuller added a pair of touchdown passes to Layton Harris, including a 23-yard strike to close the first half and put Decatur up 27-14.

      Fuller, who came off the field after Gunner Ragsdale scored with six minutes remaining, finished the night 20-for-27 for 281 yards and four scores. He added a touchdown run.

      “We had a big grudge. We hadn’t beat this team yet,” Fuller said. “They are a great football team. We had great blocking up front. David was getting open, and I just threw it to him.

      “I just think about first downs each week. You keep getting first downs, and you eventually score.”

      For the season, Fuller has thrown for 907 yards with 10 touchdowns and no interceptions in three games.

       

      “He puts a lot of time in it and takes a lot of pride in it. He’s a great competitor,” Coach Fuller said. “I love that he’s our quarterback. He’s got some great receivers. He’d be the first to tell you that he can’t do it by himself. If we protect well up front for him, run the ball well, our receivers can make some great plays.”

      Including Ryder Partridge picking up a fumble recovery on the Jaguars’ first drive, Decatur forced three turnovers. Shay Dubois picked off a pass at the 5-yard line just before the end of the first quarter to turn Heritage away.

      Then on Heritage’s first possession of the third quarter, Landry Phipps picked off a pass at the line of scrimmage.

      “If you’re plus three [on turnovers], you’re going to have a good chance to win,” Coach Fuller said. “We harp a lot on ball security.”

      At 3-0, Decatur will now head to Graham next week to face another team that had its number last year.

      “We’re not hanging our hat on being 3-0. Just focusing on next week and the next play,” Roman Fuller said.
